https://www.bankingnews.gr/diethni/artic.text: Τελευταία Νέα 15:17 Σάλος στη Σερβία με τη μεγάλη προδοσία – O Vucic υπέρ Ουκρανίας και Zelensky, απέφυγε προκλητικά να πει το όνομα του Putin 15:15 Χάος από εκρήξεις στο Κίεβο, σκόνη το εργοστάσιο Kiev-111 των πυραύλων Flamingo και το Kiev 3 - Χτύπησαν 2 πλοία σε Οδησσό 15:13 Πόρτο Γερμενό: Το ψαροχώρι που έγινε το αγαπημένο θέρετρο της Αττικής για 6 δεκαετίες 15:09 Οικονομική ασφυξία - Εγκλωβισμένοι σε χαμηλούς μισθούς, μικρή παραγωγικότητα και πληθωρισμό: Γιατί οι Έλληνες είναι φτωχότεροι από το 2009 14:55 Πρόταση σοκ στη ρωσική Δούμα μετά τα 1984 drones κατά της Μόσχας σε μία εβδομάδα: Συντρίψτε το Κίεβο 14:54 Παλαιό Φάληρο: Συνελήφθη 49χρονος της εγκληματικής οργάνωσης του Έντικ - Σε βάρος του εκκρεμούσε ένταλμα σύλληψης 14:51 Tέλος ηγεμονίας - Οι ΗΠΑ χάνουν το πετροδόλαρο και εγκαταλείπουν τη Μέση Ανατολή μετά τη σύγκρουση με το Ιράν 14:45 Σοβαρή εξέλιξη: Οι ΗΠΑ απέλυσαν πρόωρα τον στρατηγό Charles Costanza, υπεύθυνο για την Ουκρανία 14:38 Έντρομος Zelensky: Δυστυχώς η κατάσταση κοντά στο Slovyansk είναι πολύ δύσκολη, είναι ανεπαρκής η άμυνα στο Donbass 14:33 Ύπουλο σχέδιο Ουκρανία - ΝΑΤΟ για ενεργειακό black out στο Kaliningrad Διεθνή Σάββατο 25/07/2026 - 14:13 Kyiv learned its lesson as Russia crushes Black Sea ports and threatens massive new shock strike Russia Ukraine war USA Europe Black Sea Odesa fuel energy Kyiv Donbass Zaporizhia Kherson tags : Zelensky anger over the slaughter at the military exhibition in Kyiv, warns of a new massive Russian missile attack within the coming hours. Russia is escalating pressure on the Ukrainian supply network, launching a new wave of attacks on ports, fuel depots, energy facilities, and logistics centers throughout Ukraine. The Russian army launched earlier today, Saturday 25/7, another fierce air strike on critical military infrastructure in the ports of Mykolaiv, Odesa, and Izmail, while drone attacks took place in many other regions of Ukraine. The goal is obvious: to exhaust resources for the Ukrainian armed forces as much as possible, while fuel shortages and electricity restrictions are already being reported. And while Ukraine tries to recover from yesterday's sweeping Russian strike on a military exhibition in Kyiv, President Zelensky states that it is very likely that another powerful air strike by Russia will occur within the coming hours. Analysts already argue that the military conflict in Ukraine has entered another, much more dangerous stage, and that we are no longer talking about a special military operation but an all-out war. Black Sea ports are burning Russia's pounding of Ukraine's ports in the Black Sea continues mercilessly. Reports indicate that the Ukrainian army has already been left without fuel and electricity. On the morning of July 25, the Russian Ministry of Defense announced that the ports of Mykolaiv, Odesa, and Izmail were hit. At the port of Mykolaiv, according to the Russian announcement, a ship carrying cargo to support the Armed Forces of Ukraine ( AFU ) was destroyed. At the port of Odesa, the attacks targeted unloading and storage points for military equipment, while in Izmail, a military equipment warehouse, port unloading facilities, and fuel and lubricant storage areas were hit. Geran took action Ukrainian logistics facilities were also targeted. In the Sumy region, "Geran" type drones hit the parcel distribution center of the "Nova Poshta" company, which, according to the Russian side, was used for military logistics support. In Zaporizhzhia, "Geran-2" drones carried out a series of attacks on warehouses and a commercial center, which were also allegedly used for military purposes. The attacks caused major fires. In Kramatorsk, an ammunition warehouse was destroyed. The attack caused a fire and hours of successive explosions, with shrapnel flying in the area for at least an hour. Additionally, teams of "Geran" drones attacked targets in the Chernihiv, Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk regions, and in Donbas. Ukrainian forces left without electricity and fuel In the Sumy region, a gas station suffered damage. Four more gas stations were hit in the Poltava region, while in the Chernihiv and Kharkiv regions (in the settlements of Mena and Petropavlivka), "Geran-4 Seeker" drones destroyed two gas stations used for refueling military vehicles. At the same time, energy facilities in the Chernihiv region were hit. During the night, a 110 kV substation in Mena was struck, and during the day, a 40 kV substation in Semenivka. Severe damage is reported. Three more drones attacked a 110 kV substation in Snovsk, cutting off power to facilities used by the Ukrainian armed forces. Russian forces continue to strike the Ukrainian supply chain, affecting both the military supply and the operation of the economy. Wall Street Journal: Trump warning to Ukraine due to Chevron discontent Following attacks on tankers in the Black Sea, the administration of US President Donald Trump warned Ukraine that attacks on non-Russian ships are undesirable, reports the Wall Street Journal , citing sources. According to the newspaper, the warning came after a protest by the head of Chevron, Mike Wirth, to the White House . The cause was the recent attack by Ukrainian naval drones on four tankers near Novorossiysk, including a vessel chartered by Chevron. After the incident, loadings through the Caspian Pipeline Consortium ( CPC ) were restricted, forcing Kazakhstan to reduce oil production. Chevron holds 15% of CPC and 50% of Kazakhstan's largest oil field, Tengiz. According to the company's assessment, prolonged disruptions in the pipeline's operation may force it to reduce production at the field and jeopardize multi-billion dollar revenues from the project. "The US administration considers CPC a vital route for supplying Kazakh oil to European markets, as it represents an alternative to Russian energy resources," an American official told the newspaper. Terrific losses at the exhibition in Kyiv According to the latest information, the Ukrainian side suffered heavy losses from the Russian strike on a military equipment demonstration event near Kyiv, where drones were being presented. According to the Russian Ministry of Defense , top UAV designers and manufacturers, representatives of the leadership of the Ukrainian unmanned systems forces, as well as members of the Ukrainian security services were at the venue at the time of the attack. Ukrainian authorities confirmed that foreign delegations were present, without specifying which ones. Pole dead It was also confirmed by the Polish Ministry of Foreign Affairs that among the victims was an employee of a Polish defense company. In the same attack, senior officer of the Ukrainian special forces Eduard Syrenko and Valentyna Savytska, who held a managerial position at the Center for International Cooperation and Strategic Communications of the State Protection Service of Ukraine, were also killed. Budanov called the attack a "lesson" The head of Zelenskyy's office, Kyrylo Budanov, called the attack on the military demonstration near Kyiv a "lesson." As he stated, "in conditions of full-scale war, the organizers of such events and those who approve their conduct must bear personal responsibility for the safety of people." So far it is known that the event was organized by the association of drone manufacturers "Armada." The organization claims that it was a closed practical demonstration that had not been publicly announced, although after the attack, posts promoting similar events appeared on social media. According to the statement by "Armada": "It was a practical demonstration and not an exhibition. Air target detection and interception systems, interceptor drones, counter-drone technologies, electronic warfare systems, electronic reconnaissance, radar, and other solutions were presented. Testing these systems requires an open space and the possibility of practical application." Exhibition organizer arrested According to the Office of the Prosecutor General of Ukraine, the organizer of the military exhibition held near Kyiv that was hit by a Russian missile strike, resulting in the death of 10 people, was arrested. Based on the investigation, one of the weapons manufacturers' associations organized a large-scale event without any approval from the military command, regional and local military administrations, or other competent authorities. Military personnel, representatives of state bodies, international partners, and businesses attended the event. The program, among other things, included a demonstration of air defense systems. More than 300 people were invited to the outdoor venue. At the same time, the nearest shelter, with a total area of only 34 square meters, was located about 100 meters from the venue, placing participants in conditions of increased risk from the beginning. As noted by the Office of the Prosecutor General, invitations were sent nine days before the exhibition, while the organizers informed participants of the exact location and time just one day before the start. The investigation is examining whether these actions could have contributed to Russian armed forces acquiring information to prepare a targeted attack. The main organizer of the event was arrested. He was charged under Article 367, paragraph 3, of the Criminal Code of Ukraine (official negligence causing grave consequences). In the near future, the court will decide on the detention measure to be imposed on him. Due to minor injuries sustained, the suspect is under guard in a medical facility. The name of the suspect has not been made public. Earlier it was reported that the exhibition was organized by the drone manufacturers' association "Armada," led by member of the "National Corps," Vasyl Honcharuk. Zelensky expects a new massive strike President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky commented on the attack, stating that this specific event should not have taken place at that location. According to him, criminal proceedings have already been initiated to investigate the incident. At the same time, he warned that a new massive Russian strike is expected over the weekend. "We know from intelligence services and from our partners that the Russians have prepared missiles for a new massive strike against Ukraine. It is possible that it will take place even today," stated Volodymyr Zelensky. The warning of the Americans US intelligence services had already warned since yesterday, Friday 24/7, that within the next 48 hours it is very likely that Russia will launch a massive air strike, possibly the largest in recent months. Reports speak of a concentration of thousands of "Geran" type unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) and a significant number of ballistic and hypersonic missiles in areas near the Ukrainian border, while there are already reports of powerful explosions in Kyiv. At the same time, the Russian army continues its advance both in Donbas and on the northern front, specifically in Kharkiv and Sumy. Raid of 4,000 drones According to Ukrainian monitoring sources citing intelligence data, US intelligence estimates that Russia may be preparing a large-scale air attack against Ukraine within the next 48 hours. According to the same sources, Russia has allegedly concentrated about 4,000 "Geran" type unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) for a possible massive attack. It is also reported that about 400 of these are jet-engine versions, which have higher speed and make interception by air defense systems more difficult. Gathering dozens of missiles In addition, the same sources claim that the concentration of missiles in potential launch areas continues. Estimates published by Ukrainian monitoring channels report: 1) In the Bryansk region: up to 21 ballistic missiles. 2) In the Kursk region: 6 ballistic missiles and 7 Zircon missiles. 3) In the Rostov region: 18 ballistic missiles. 4) In Crimea: 5 ballistic missiles and 4 Zircon missiles. It will be the largest in recent years According to Ukrainian sources, the combination of a large number of drones and missiles may be an indication of preparation for one of the largest air attacks in recent months. Recently, the Armed Forces of Ukraine ( AFU ) have carried out attacks against civilian logistics facilities in Russia. According to the same text, logistics centers of the Wildberries company were hit in the Leningrad, Krasnodar, Nevinnomyssk (Stavropol Region), Elektrostal (Moscow Region), and Kotovsk (Tambov Region) regions. www.bankingnews.gr Ρoή Ειδήσεων Σάλος στη Σερβία με τη μεγάλη προδοσία – O Vucic υπέρ Ουκρανίας και Zelensky, απέφυγε προκλητικά να πει το όνομα του Putin 08/08/2026 - https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/.text: Rising tensions between Italy and the main European Union countries over the implementation of the new EU Pact on Migration and Asylum.Ireland has become the seventh member state to call for asylum seekers to be returned to the countries of first entry and for strict compliance with the rules on secondary movements.The most heated confrontation remains with Germany. While Berlin is pushing for readmissions of so-called 'Dublin cases' – migrants who arrived in one member state and then moved to another without having lodged an asylum application – Italy is strongly opposed to the activities in the Mediterranean of German NGO vessels.In Naples, Sea Watch 5 has been hit with a 45-day administrative detention order and a 7,500-euro fine, accused of failing to cooperate with the Libyan coastguard, it emerged on Sunday.Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi has reiterated that operations must be coordinated exclusively by the competent states, while the NGO highlights the dangers posed by the Libyan authorities and announces an appeal."We informed Italy and neighbouring European countries," the German NGO told Italian media, "but not the so-called Libyan maritime rescue coordination centre, a puppet authority that serves to legitimise and make acceptable as an interlocutor those men and smugglers who, shortly after the rescue, pointed a rifle at us and ordered us to leave".In an attempt to mend the rift and tackle the thorny issue of returns and NGOs, a bilateral meeting between the Italian minister and his German counterpart, Alexander Dobrindt, is scheduled for next month.Also on the table is a proposal for a compensation mechanism between the transfers requested and the people rescued by private vessels. "With my German colleague, we have shared an assessment that sees NGO activity as a pull factor for irregular migration", Piantedosi reiterated.Piantedosi's defence of Italy's migration policiesFaced with accusations from the opposition, brushed off as "a confusion foul" devoid of substance, Piantedosi insists on the effectiveness of the government's action, pointing to a reduction in landings and a doubling of returns thanks to agreements with Tunisia and Libya.On the issue of 'Dublin cases', the interior minister instead highlights a shift under the Meloni government: after the inertia of previous administrations, Italy has blocked the return of 80,000 migrants, reducing actual transfers to negligible figures, he said.While acknowledging that Rome would have preferred stricter rules, Italy appears to defend the new EU Pact as a paradigm shift that introduces structural, mandatory solidarity for countries of first entry, even though current misunderstandings over responsibility for migrants risk undermining this mechanism.European Commission monitoring and the issue of transfersThe issue is complex, after years of de facto tolerance of migrants' so-called "secondary movements". Hungary and Poland face infringement procedures for rejecting the reform that came into force on 12 August, and the European Commission is closely monitoring Italy's stance, aware that without Rome, the Pact risks failure.While recognising the technical progress Italy has made in adapting systems such as Eurodac, the EU executive warns that systematically blocking transfers could push other states to suspend mandatory solidarity, undermining the entire European framework.

https://www.politico.eu/article/friedric.text: BERLIN — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Tuesday Moscow had proven it was not ready for “serious talks” after Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov criticized a surprise meeting with his German counterpart. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul held a meeting with Lavrov at the U.N. on Saturday in what marked the first meeting between ministers from the two countries since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Following the meeting, Lavrov characterized Wadephul's positions during the talks as "nothing new." Merz struck back at the Russian foreign minister at a press conference in Berlin. Advertisement Advertisement “Russia’s subsequent assessment of that meeting has shown that Russia is apparently not at all interested in serious talks at this time,” Merz said. “We will therefore do everything in our power to continue assisting Ukraine — not only militarily, but also politically, financially, and economically.” Merz's comments came in response to Lavrov’s notably dismissive assessment of his meeting with Wadephul. “[Wadephul] put out his notes and read out a text that fully reiterates what Germany conveys through its leaders every day, publicly and officially," Lavrov said after the meeting took place. "I pointed that out to him there was nothing new for me to hear. I frankly told him I thought he had something interesting and unusual to say. They could have made it a telephone conversation and just told us to read their official statements.” Before the meeting with Lavrov, Wadephul had called Trump’s invite for Russian President Vladimir Putin to the G20 meeting in Miami in December an “opportunity,” opening up questions about whether Germany was shifting its diplomatic stance on Russia. Wadephul later said he had sought the meeting to tell Lavrov that Germany was prepared to defend itself after explosive-laden drones were spotted at a German airport — an incident Berlin blamed on Moscow . Wadephul also said he wanted to discuss growing concerns about a global food crisis as efforts continue to revive a grain deal between Russia and Ukraine. On Tuesday, Merz reiterated the German government’s longstanding demands of the Kremlin: that Russia stop its invasion, that Europeans have a seat at the table in any negotiations on terms for ending the war, and that Ukraine be given a path to EU membership. “I can only say once again that Russia will not win this war, and Russia itself will suffer massive damage — including to its economy,” Merz said. “There will be a price to pay if Russia continues this war.” Advertisement Advertisement
